   SWORN WRITTEN DIRECT TESTIMONY FOR SOAH HEARING ON THE MERITS
     ONCOR and LCRA TSC Bell County East to Big Hill 765 kV Transmission Project
                         SOAH Docket 473-26-16349
                           PUC TX Docket #59475


Objection to Proposed V-8 Route and Protest Respective to Parcel 4201.3

Honorable Judge:

I respectfully request the following testimony with Exhibit 1 enclosed herein be admitted as
evidence. Information was previously provided in my position statement in the PUC TX 59475
Filing.
My name is M. Rex Emerson and I am testifying against the Proposed V-8 Route. My address is
269 Treasure Hills Rd Kerrville, Texas 78028. My wife, Kelli A Emerson, and I own Tract
4201.3 located at 350 CR154 Brady, Texas.
I graduated from Texas A&M University with a Bachelors of Business Administration and
subsequently obtained my Juris Doctor from St. Mary’s University. I am employed as a Senior
District Judge for the State of Texas.
We purchased this property in 2012 with the intent to develop a family ranch for agricultural,
recreational and hunting use. We were in the process of acquiring additional acreage when we
were served with notice of the proposed 765 kV V-8 transmission line route. We have stopped
all expansion plans.
The proposed V-8 route will bisect our 168.61-acre ranch for approximately 2660 feet, dividing
our property and substantially reducing its utility, market value, and overall integrity. The center
of the proposed transmission line will be approximately 525 feet from our residence, 470 feet
from the residence well, 440 feet from the barn, 240 feet from the windmill well, and will pass
directly over our stock pond. Each structure is metal-clad and lies within the unsafe 500 to 700-
foot recommended setoff distance from high-voltage transmission lines. (Exhibit 1)
The transmission line and minimum 500-foot LCRA-mandated construction setback will render
35.5% of our land unusable for improvements or development. (Exhibit 1)
For 14 years, we have managed wildlife on our ranch, including, but not limited to, white-tailed
deer, feral hogs, varmints, migratory birds, quail, and turkeys. As you know, turkeys and quail
are particularly sensitive to environmental changes. In addition, we have red-tailed hawk nests
located on our property. The right-of-way construction will result in the removal of numerous
mature oak trees, several of which are over 100 years old. In addition, significant native brush
would be removed. Multiple wildlife feeders with solar panels are located less than the 600’
minimum setoff from the proposed high voltage transmission line route. To further complicate
the issue, the bisecting route significantly reduces our options for feeder placement thereby
effectively reducing by at least 50% our feral hog control and hunting opportunities.
Constructing the 765 kV V-8 transmission line would be detrimental to our wildlife
management.
The transmission line will pass directly over our stock pond. It is my understanding that a stock
pond is not compatible with a high-voltage transmission line right-of-way and would have to be
                                                                                       Page 1 of 5
 removed. The loss of the pond will directly affect our agricultural and wildlife operations and
will cost a significant sum of money to replace.
The center of the transmission line will be approximately 240 feet from our windmill well. The
windmill is almost 100 years old and is constructed of metal. In addition, our plans to upgrade
the pump from leathers to solar will be thwarted by the 600-foot minimum setback required for
solar panels from high-voltage transmission lines. In the best-case scenario, the windmill will
likely transfer “nuisance” shocks and require higher operating costs, and in the worst-case
scenario, we will lose our well.
The proximity of the transmission line to our residence raises concerns about exposure to
electromagnetic fields, constant 50 decibel noise disrupting peace and quiet, a visual nuisance,
loss of dark skies, loss of a beautiful view, and an increased fire risk. Essentially, a general
degradation of the quality of life. Discussions with neighbors who own or lease property with
high-voltage transmission lines included a detailed education that caused me to be concerned
about electrified fences and gates, as well as nuisance shocks.
The market value of our property will be significantly affected. I have extensively researched
similar rural properties for sale and discussed the issues with multiple experienced reputable
realtors and formed an educated opinion as the property owner that our property will lose 35 to
50 percent of its fair market value.
The PUCT regulatory standards were created when much lower voltage transmission lines were
the standard. It is my understanding that Texas has never used a 765 kV transmission line, yet the
routing process is no more rigorous than that for a 345 kV transmission line. The proposed 765
kV transmission line requires heavier conductors and larger support towers, with much larger
vertical and horizontal right-of-way requirements than those of other existing lines. In addition,
they generate significantly larger electromagnetic fields than any other line currently in use in
Texas, yet none of the LCRA or ONCOR guidelines seem to reflect the more than 100 percent
increase in transmission line voltage.
The proposed Alternate V-8 route deviates into the far northern segment of the proposed route
network, thereby creating a more circuitous route for the project. This is a significant deviation
from the Best Meets Route. This unnecessary deviation will increase the length of the
transmission line thereby increasing construction costs and material use.
In addition, it is my understanding that the proposed Alternate V-8 route will significantly
impact the safety and operations of the Curtis Field Airport located in Brady, Texas. I have
personally observed both civilian and military aircraft utilizing this air field.




                                                                                         Page 2 of 5
 Alternate route V-8 imposes an undue burden on the landowner by materially impairing the use,
enjoyment, access, and operational control of our property. The route interferes with agricultural
and recreational use, creates safety concerns, and divides the property, thereby fundamentally
altering its character and causing a significant and permanent loss of 35.5 percent of our land
and a fair-market loss of 35 to 50 percent of its value. (see Exhibit 1)


My name is Melvin Rex Emerson. My date of birth is August 30, 1960, and my address is 269
Treasure Hills Road, Kerrville, Texas 78028 in Kerr County, Texas. I declare under penalty of
perjury that the foregoing is true and correct.
Executed in Kerr County, State of Texas on the 2nd day of June, 2026.




M. Rex Emerson
